terms.definition: Text changes made by fixed rules and word lists, without asking a language model. Here it means the existing saved version of the OCR after those rules; it can still contain mistakes.

The particular saved model responses chosen for evaluation or for a proposed reading version. Other responses, failed attempts and alternatives remain saved; selection alone does not mean a person has approved them.
A correction needed to restore the actual wording or meaning, such as a wrong name, number, missing phrase or negation. Merely changing spacing or appearance does not count.
Test examples deliberately given missing or unrelated source evidence, to check that the model asks for review instead of guessing. They are tests of behavior, not ordinary historical passages.
New serious errors introduced by cleanup into text that was previously correct, such as changing a person, amount, date, bill number or the word “not.”
Optical character recognition: software that turns a scanned page into searchable text. Its output can misread letters, numbers and layout.
The original machine-read text, preserved exactly as collected, including its errors.
A separate, corrected version intended for reading and listening. It keeps links to the original text and scan, and does not replace them.
Supported by what the original page actually shows, with a link back to that evidence. Plausible wording alone is not enough.

Recorded expectations about what the source supports, prepared for a check. They may be provisional AI observations or human judgments; the record must say which. They are not automatically verified history.
A saved collection of the exact passages, context, image references and settings to be used in a test.
Save a fixed, identifiable version before a test so that all models use the same material and later changes are visible.
A file or text fingerprint. Matching fingerprints show that the bytes match the recorded version; they do not prove that the historical text is correct.
Changes to the project’s published base text or accepted records. A proposed correction does not automatically change these records.
A small, limited trial used to learn whether a larger workflow is worth pursuing. It is not permission to process the whole collection.
The project’s still-open decision about whether further OCR cleanup is worth its total cost, and for which uses.
A small set chosen to reveal particular strengths and failures. Its results do not estimate the error rate of the whole collection.
Groups of examples chosen to cover different conditions, such as corpus part, document type or OCR damage.
The complete collection being studied: here, the five collected parts of the 39th Congress, first session.
Kept separate from examples used to develop or adjust the method, so a later test is less influenced by prior tuning.
A few examples used to clarify how a person or method should judge cases. They are not automatically an independent final test.
Comparison examples used to check behavior, including unchanged text or deliberately missing evidence. Their exact purpose should be stated.
Text-to-speech: software that reads text aloud. Checking the text for likely spoken errors is different from actually listening to generated audio.
Retrieval-augmented generation: an AI system first finds passages, then uses them as evidence when answering a question.
Finding relevant passages in the collection, using words, meaning or filters.
Adding proposed information to passages, such as a speaker, date, subject or bill reference. Each claim needs its own evidence.
How closely the proposed reading preserves what the original scan says, including names, numbers and qualifications.
Changes to actual wording or meaning that the supplied source evidence does not justify.
Whether the reading preserves meaning-bearing details such as names, numbers, dates, negations and whole sentences. A serious change in any of these is a critical error.
A person examines the passage and source to resolve an uncertainty or check a proposed change.
The service or local software that runs a language model and returns its response.
Running a model on an input to generate a response. It does not mean the response has been verified.
Individual requests sent to a model, including ones that fail or time out. A retry is another attempt.
The pieces of text a model reads or writes, often words or parts of words. Token limits are not the same as word limits.
Surrounding text and other information supplied with a passage. It can help interpretation but must not be used to invent missing wording.
The pieces of text the model is allowed to generate in its reply.
A request that has not completed within the allowed time. It may require checking whether the model is still working.
Text cut off because an input or reply exceeds a limit. A cut-off reply is not a complete successful result.
Tests that saved work can be recovered after an interruption without losing results or accidentally repeating requests.
Continue from saved work after stopping, reusing completed compatible results rather than starting over.
Reproduce a saved transformation or result from the same recorded inputs, without asking a model again.
Saved material that can be reused when its inputs and settings still match.
A small image cut from an original scanned page. Its recorded page and position connect it to the text being checked.
Exact references connecting a claim or correction to its original passage, page and image region.
Recorded changes containing the old text, replacement text and exact location. They allow checking and reversing a correction.
The required structure and fields of a saved record or model reply. Passing this check shows correct structure, not historical correctness.
Automatic checks that data follows required rules, such as correct fields and matching source text. These checks alone do not establish historical truth.
A further test on fresh examples after choosing a method, to see whether its apparent benefit holds up.
The agreed limits on local model requests, running time, image transfers and other computer resources.
The existing version used for comparison, such as raw OCR or current static cleanup.
The extra useful improvement over the existing comparison version, after accounting for new mistakes and added effort.
A result for which the available evidence does not support a reliable answer. It is not a correct reading or permission to guess.
Explicitly declining to supply an unsupported reading or assignment and leaving it for review.
How much material the workflow completes in a measured amount of time, including the stated failures and overhead.
The actual historical passages in the test, counted once per passage. Artificial missing-image or wrong-image tests are counted separately.
A working proposal or judgment that may change after review or more evidence. It has not been adopted as a final standard.
A software connection that lets the workflow send a request to a model service and receive its response.
The program that sends the prepared requests, saves replies and tracks progress, failures and time limits.
Checks completed before a run begins, such as confirming the inputs fit the model limits and the source fingerprints match.
A coordination mechanism that allows only one participating local model request at a time, to prevent jobs from overlapping.
One request runs at a time; the next starts only after the previous request has finished or been reconciled.
A fixed set of examples and scoring rules used to compare methods. A small benchmark does not establish performance for every passage.
Words such as “not” or “never” that reverse or limit a statement. Losing one can change the historical meaning.
Using a proposed result without checking that individual result by hand. The pilot does not itself permit this for the corpus.
The pieces of text the model can take into account, including instructions, surrounding passages and the space needed for a reply.
Shortened forms such as “Mr.” or “Sec.” Preserving them avoids silently adding wording that is not printed.
The original material being checked, such as a printed page or its saved image. A proposed AI answer is separate from that original material.
The words, images or records offered to support an answer. You still need to check whether they actually support the particular claim.
The record of where material came from and what happened to it: its original page, saved versions, transformations and reviews.
A label identifying the particular source passage, including its volume part, scanned page and paragraph. It is a reference, not a correctness grade.
An identifier made from several pieces, such as volume, scanned-page number and paragraph number, so passages from different volumes are not confused.
Tied to a specific recorded source passage, page or image. That connection can be checked; it does not by itself prove an interpretation correct.
The point where one source passage or region ends and another begins. A proposed change must not accidentally include words from a different passage.
The points where one paragraph begins and ends. Preserving them means keeping separate paragraphs separate rather than joining or splitting them without support.
The particular paragraph from the original material. Nearby paragraphs provide context but are not interchangeable with the paragraph being checked.
A block of connected text, usually separated from the next block by a new line or indentation. The review keeps its original source identity.
The piece of text selected for reading or checking. It can be part of a paragraph or several connected paragraphs.
An image of the original printed page, or a recorded portion of that page, used to compare the printed words with machine-read text.
The numbered page image in the scanned volume. Its number can differ from the page number printed on the original paper.
The page number printed on the original paper. It is distinct from the scanned-image number, which may also count covers and blank pages.
The words and numbers visible on the original paper, as distinct from the machine-read text or a proposed corrected version.
A reference telling you where to find the original passage or page. A precise citation makes a claim checkable; it does not automatically make it correct.
A fingerprint for the exact saved text of one paragraph. A matching fingerprint identifies the same text version, including any OCR errors.
Connected to saved text or image bytes using a recorded fingerprint, so a different file or text version can be detected.
Information describing a file or passage, such as its page number, source, format or recorded date. Each field needs its own stated basis.
A saved record that something was received or recorded, such as an image download or a submitted review. It is not a judgment that the content is correct.
An image-sharing standard that lets a link request a full scanned page or a specific area of it. Here it is used to show the original print.
A web address pointing to a page or file. A source URL helps you open the material; it is different from a fingerprint of the saved file.
A common way computers store text as bytes, including accented letters and other symbols. A file fingerprint refers to those exact stored bytes.
A plain-text format for saving named pieces of data and lists. A schema specifies what a particular JSON record must contain; the two are different things.
The AI system that produces a response from supplied text or images. A model answer is a proposal until its evidence and accuracy have been checked.
Artificial intelligence. Here it usually means software that generates a proposed answer or reading, which can still contain mistakes.
The AI assistant doing project work, such as preparing evidence or checking results. Its judgment is not a substitute for your own answer.
The material supplied to a program or AI, such as the passage, instructions and source image. Missing input can change what the answer can support.
The answer or text produced by a program or AI, including responses later rejected. Producing an output does not mean it is correct.
The saved response exactly as the model returned it, before accepting, changing or interpreting it. A failed response is still retained.
The particular material, instructions and settings sent to a program or AI for one response. Requests can be saved so later work is traceable.
The instructions given to an AI about what to do and how to answer. Changing the prompt can change the answer.
The recorded choices controlling a run, such as the selected model, time limit and maximum reply length. Matching text alone does not mean settings match.
One recorded execution of a particular set of tasks with stated inputs, settings and limits. A run may stop with failures or unfinished work.
Processing the entire agreed collection, rather than a small test. A limited review or test does not itself authorize this larger job.
The sequence of steps used to prepare material, ask for answers, check them, save them and handle failures.
A group of passages or tasks processed together under stated limits. Completing a batch does not prove the method works for the whole collection.
The particular example or group of examples selected for examination. A small selected sample may not represent the entire collection.
Examples chosen in advance and kept in the review, including failed or unavailable results. They are not replaced with better-looking examples.
With identifying information hidden. In these model reviews, the model name is hidden while you judge the proposed text.
A review that hides specified information to reduce its influence on the judgment. Source-only grading hides model answers; hiding names alone is a different kind of review.
You can see a proposed model answer while judging it. This differs from recording your own expectations before seeing the answer.
A working AI assessment that has not been confirmed by a human. It stays separate from an actual human judgment.
A check that all intended text and images reach the model. A saved plan is not enough if the actual request leaves material out.
A suggested answer, rule or text change that has not automatically been accepted. Displaying a proposal does not apply it to the original text.
A suggested version of the text, shown for comparison with the source. It is not automatically an accepted transcription.
A full proposed text for the selected passage, rather than only a list of individual suggested changes. It still needs checking against the source.
A written rendering of the words on the original page. It may be made by a person or software; its accuracy still needs checking.
Using the exact words as given, without rewriting them. Verbatim copying of OCR can still preserve OCR mistakes.
Matching what the original print says without changing its wording or meaning. Clearer or smoother writing alone is not enough.
A correction to damaged or mistaken text. The source must support the correction; readability alone does not establish the original wording.
Not accepted under the stated check. A response can be rejected for a mechanical or formatting problem without every suggested word being historically wrong.
Approved under a stated check or review. The desk should say whether approval came from software or a person; software approval alone is not historical verification.
A decision or approved change has actually been incorporated into the project records. Merely showing a proposal does not mean it has been applied.
Keeping or reusing selected parts of an otherwise rejected response. If nothing was salvaged, the visible suggestions were not used as accepted changes.
The selected result was not produced or cannot be supplied for this review. It is a missing result, not a passing or failing historical grade.
A different example or result used in place of the originally chosen one. The fixed review does not silently replace missing results this way.
What the available evidence does not settle. The review should leave it visible rather than force a confident answer.
Not examined for the particular judgment being requested. No approval or rejection should be inferred from an unfinished review.
Judging an answer or proposed reading using the stated criteria. A software format check is different from a person checking the historical source.
The rules used to judge whether a result is acceptable, such as preserving names and numbers. They must be stated rather than silently assumed.
A rule governing how the project handles a class of cases. Agreeing with one example is not necessarily agreement to a general rule.
An investigation used to learn what happens, with conclusions kept tentative. It does not automatically satisfy final acceptance standards.
The agreed requirements that must be met before a result or method is treated as acceptable for its stated use.
The amount and kind of checking you agree to do. It does not imply a promise to keep grading later examples or to approve a larger run.
One specifically requested set of review work. Completing it does not automatically commit you to another set.
The maximum time for all the samples together, rather than that much time for each sample. You can stop earlier.
A saved set of questions and supporting material for you to examine. Registering it does not record a human answer.
Answers saved so you can return to them later. A draft has not been submitted as a completed review.
Send your answers as a recorded review for an agent to read and apply within their scope. Opening a definition does not submit anything.
A later recorded version of an answer or document. Earlier submitted answers remain preserved rather than silently overwritten.
Still waiting for the relevant action, such as your review or an agent applying it. A pending website entry may already have been answered in chat.
Saved earlier reviews and decisions. These are records to consult, not a request to answer the same questions again.
The name or label you enter to identify your review. It is not a password or proof of your historical expertise.
The particular words, images or records offered to justify an answer. Check that they support that answer, not merely a related topic.
A specific stretch of original text identified within its source paragraph or passage. It must preserve the exact words and source reference.
A position counted from the beginning of a specified text. For text evidence here, positions count Unicode characters, not printed page numbers.
The saved details connecting material to its origin, versions and processing steps. It helps reconstruct what was actually shown or changed.
Here, a list of names or subjects followed by page references. The numbers point to other pages; they are not necessarily years.
A tax on goods imported into a country. A speaker may support or oppose a tariff; the definition does not judge that argument.
A tariff described as high enough to discourage or prevent imports. The phrase alone does not prove that a particular tariff had that effect.
In a tariff discussion, a tax charged on goods. Elsewhere the same word can mean a responsibility; the surrounding passage determines the meaning.
Goods brought into a country from abroad, or the act of bringing them in. This is different from goods sent out of the country.
Money received by a government, often from taxes or duties. The definition does not verify any particular amount claimed in a speech.
An older spelling of percent: an amount out of every hundred. For example, fifty per cent means fifty out of a hundred.
A type of sorghum grown for its long, branched fibers, which are used to make brooms. It is not ordinary maize grown for eating.
An old expression for a distraction that draws attention away from a larger issue. Explaining the expression does not establish whether the speaker is right.
aliases: thrown a tub to the whale

terms.definition: A printed stage direction referring to the presiding officer’s gavel. It can mark a procedural signal, such as the end of a speaking turn; the surrounding passage supplies its meaning.
In congressional proceedings, a proposal to create, change or repeal a law. A bill being discussed is not necessarily an enacted law.
A proposed change to a bill or other text. A statement that an amendment was not agreed to means that proposed change was not adopted.
A smaller group of legislators assigned to consider particular subjects or carry out specific work for their chamber.
Legislative provision of public money for a specified purpose. It concerns permission to spend funds, not proof that every listed payment occurred.
Defensive structures or works, such as forts. An index entry about them points to discussion elsewhere in the volume.
A payment made under stated eligibility rules, often for military service, disability or a dependent. A proposed pension is not proof that someone received it.
A formal proposal for action or a statement by a legislative body. Its legal effect depends on the kind of resolution and what was adopted.
The recorded business of a legislative body, including speeches, motions and votes. Nearby proceedings may concern different subjects or speakers.
One of the two houses of Congress—the House of Representatives or the Senate—or the room where that body meets.
The ending of a legislative meeting or session. It marks a proceeding boundary but does not by itself supply a date.
An official who handles legislative records and procedural duties. The title alone does not always identify the particular person holding it.
A legal procedure for asking a court to review whether a person is being held lawfully. Here the whole phrase has this meaning, unlike the project term corpus.
People or businesses that bring goods into a country from abroad. Their statements in a speech still need to be checked against the source.
Made up for a test or demonstration. A synthetic passage is not an original historical source and cannot become a historical label.
The particular material, question and limits covered by a task or decision. Approval within one scope does not automatically apply to other work.
Limited in advance, for example by the number of examples, requests, minutes or permitted actions. Unused capacity is not permission to expand the work.
Added together across the stated group or period, including earlier counted work. Restarting does not make already-used time or requests disappear.
An order fixed in advance using recorded fingerprints. It keeps selection consistent; it is not a ranking of which answers are better.
Recorded before the new model answer was seen. This timing alone does not establish whether the observation is accurate.
A recorded note about what someone or an AI sees in source material. The record must say who checked it and what remains uncertain.
Permission, under specified rules, to send certain mail without the sender paying ordinary postage. Who had this permission and what mail it covered depended on the law at the time.

An identifying number for legislation from the House of Representatives. In these old index entries, read the printed prefix with the nearby word bill or resolution; the prefix alone does not show the measure’s type or whether it became law.
An identifying number for legislation from the Senate. Read the prefix with the surrounding entry to identify the measure; its number alone does not show whether it became law.

In this historical expression, a distraction or pretext that hides the real purpose. It is unrelated to the project’s phrase blind review. The definition explains the speaker’s expression without endorsing the claim.
Reading a proposed approach and giving feedback before it is used.
One small, fixed experiment aimed at answering one question.
An AI reading made from a page image without showing it the OCR or proposed corrections.
One AI response that proposes corrections and reports problems it notices in the supplied text. It is a single response, not a second independent check.
A check for discrepancies between supplied material and the evidence it is meant to represent.
An earlier proposed result retained so it can be inspected without changing its original bytes.
No problem was reported within the part that was inspected.
Some of the assigned material was not fully examined.
The available evidence does not settle a reading or claim.
A sequence of characters copied exactly from the identified text.
Locations in text calculated by software from a matching quote.
Rules specifying the information a program receives and the response it may return.
A separate technical evaluation of the proposed process, performed outside the work being evaluated.
Mistakes that can occur together because two answers share a model, method or other influence.
A request sent without carrying conversation history from an earlier request.
Checking that an image region lines up with its intended location in the correct source page.
Linking a result to the specific source material and positions that support it.
A fixed limit on resources such as request count, time, tokens or image bytes.
Checks that fields and evidence agree in meaning, beyond whether the response has the required format.
Saving the original response before interpreting or validating it.
Stopping the model service from continuing a request, rather than only stopping the client from waiting.
Checks performed by the surrounding software using frozen inputs and evidence.
A short label used to refer to a particular record.
A condition that must stay true throughout a process.
Connecting previously separate program parts so they work together.
The conclusion of an evaluation, with its stated scope and limits.
Software that marks text for further checking when specified patterns or signals are present.
Recorded signals or checks that describe a program input, result or problem.
An explicit list of fields or actions that a process permits.
Text produced from an original through recorded edits or transformations.
A reading of the source recorded separately from the output being evaluated. Its trust depends on who read it, the evidence and any uncertainty.
A durable record of attempts, replies and state changes.
A software package or component another program needs.
Software that decides when queued work should run.
Software development kit: a collection of tools or libraries used to build software.
A fingerprint calculated from exact source bytes, used to detect changes rather than establish historical truth.
Reusable code that applies specified rules without asking an AI model.
Information appearing in an input where the study design says it should be withheld.
Agreement between a result’s declared status and the information it contains.
An attempt to stop requested work; evidence is needed to determine which work actually stopped.
Matching responses produced by the same AI model.
A step-by-step example showing how a process works.
Written to explain a possible format or behavior, rather than presented as an observed result.
Only part of a response, shown to explain a particular detail.
Marked for further inspection; the mark alone does not establish an error.
Information used to trace or check how an example was recorded, such as its source identifiers and file fingerprints.
A piece of text grouped by the original OCR software. It may be an index line or part of an entry rather than a complete prose paragraph.
Information connecting the displayed example to its original material and saved files.
A readable tour of completed work and its remaining limits.
Using programmed rules and word lists instead of generating an AI answer.
A small test program that sends prepared responses. It does not run a language model.
The required collection of formatting, code checks and tests before a change is committed.
Joining parts split across a printed line ending. A proposed join can still be wrong.
The answer bytes returned by a server; their format alone does not establish correctness.
The exact network reply, saved before its contents are interpreted.
Flags pointing to material for later checking; they are not confirmed errors.
A request intended to return the full assigned reading and supported edits together.
Printed words in brackets describing proceedings or reactions; their wording should remain traceable.
Saved observations about whether the owned test process stopped.
Recorded facts about current processes, queue, logs and model identity before a send.
The selected backend’s actual steps for rendering text and resizing or dividing images before model input.
The installed software service that loads and runs the model.
Whether the selected software accepts and handles the required request and response format.
A specific verified readiness record for the frozen run; it is separate from the human’s permission.
The rule used to represent text as bytes; invalid bytes must not silently become invented text.
One request at a time, without overlap.
The total elapsed-time limit including setup, requests and reporting.
Agreement with the original historical evidence, beyond merely passing software checks.
The connections that move requests and results between software components.
The exact text and image representation supplied to a model before it generates a response.
The program coordinating work done by another program.
A program or thread carrying out an assigned request.
The original returned data before it is checked or interpreted.
A calculation based on dividing an image into blocks for model input; a hypothetical calculation is not a backend measurement.
Looking for a form in a saved dictionary. A match does not prove the historical spelling.
The suggested text to put in place of an exact original quote; it remains unaccepted until reviewed.
The short passage chosen from part five of this study. This label identifies the same selected passage across its saved inputs and results.
A model’s own list of what it inspected and what remains uncertain. It is part of that same answer, not an independent second opinion.
The dividing lines between the passage to repair and nearby writing supplied only to help interpret it. Nearby writing must not be appended to the passage.
Words or characters that earlier checks did not mark as suspicious. Absence of a warning does not establish that the text is correct.
Proposed changes made by repeatable software rules rather than a language model, such as joining a word split across lines.
The format identifying where a concern belongs in the original text: a quoted span or the entire paragraph.
Response-format rules in which one field controls what another field may contain. For example, choosing a whole paragraph can require an empty quote.
Software that rejects an answer when required fields, source links or text-reconstruction rules disagree. Passing these checks alone does not prove the historical wording.
Starting a request when the model needs to be loaded for that session. Loading time is part of the elapsed time reported here.
Small pieces of text or other encoded input counted by the model software. Token counts depend on how that software prepares the request.
The assumed share of passages sent to a particular cleanup or checking method. Here these are scenario assumptions, not measured error frequencies.
Additional attempts or human/software corrections after an initial attempt. Its amount and time have not been measured for the collection.
A measurement of how this installed model software actually converts the complete text and image into input, and whether that complete input fits.
Permission for one described test to proceed without first having a complete measurement of whether its text and image input fits. It supplies no permission for other requests.
A narrowly specified change to a check normally required before sending a request. It applies only to the action described in the decision.
A recorded permission that can be consumed by only one attempted request. A failed or unclear result does not automatically replenish it.
The list of work waiting or already claimed, checked to avoid starting competing model operations.
A shared software safeguard allowing only one owner to perform the protected operation at a time. Here it helps prevent overlapping model requests.
A change specified against the exact original machine-read text, rather than against a later cleaned version.
The recorded original text and replacement for each proposed change. Applying the complete list should recreate the proposed reading.
Requirements for what an answer must contain and how its fields and proposed text must agree. They do not establish historical accuracy.
Uncertainties attached to an entire passage when a smaller exact quotation cannot identify the issue. They should remain visible without inventing a reading.
Cases where the answer leaves the proposed text empty and explains why it cannot supply a supported complete reading.
The saved submitted-feedback list the coding agent checks when work resumes. Saving a draft does not add it to this list.
A running program started and tracked for this particular operation, so its exit can be checked without controlling unrelated programs.
Time cutoffs shared by several steps, so each step receives only the remaining time rather than a fresh full allowance.
The share of attempts that produce a result usable for the intended task under its checks. It has not yet been established for this cleanup method.
The written instruction and data strings before the model software adds its own framing and processes the image.
A number used to report or flag an observation, rather than a proven capacity limit or a rule that blocks the request.
Fingerprints of the exact software files and request bytes, used to detect changes between preparation and execution.
Save the current answers under the current reviewer name before opening the name field for another reviewer. Saved answers can be restored later under the original name.
The concrete result or required behavior used for comparison. Its label should explain whether it comes from an agreed rule, a reviewed reference or an authored illustration.
The result that the process really returned, kept unchanged even when incomplete or rejected. If it has not run, no actual output exists.
A response label meaning that the model reports no issue in the inspected scope. It does not independently establish correctness.
A response label reporting that the image does not clearly establish the wording. It describes uncertainty in the model’s evidence.
The response field listing issues the model says remain unresolved after its self-check.
A proposed approach where the model returns the complete assigned passage and uncertainty, while software derives the recorded text differences. It is a design option, not an accuracy guarantee.
Changes found by comparing two saved text strings in software. They describe how strings differ, not whether the scan supports a change.
A rule for matching corresponding portions of two texts. Repeated or reordered wording can allow several matches, so the match may be uncertain.
Links from an entire proposed paragraph to its original paragraph and scan, without claiming that every changed character has a uniquely identified source location.
Software preparation and testing using saved or invented data, without sending a model request.
A process in two parts: repeatable software cleanup and detection first, followed by image-based inspection of selected targets. Some apparently clean text is also audited.
A later check using the source image and context to examine a word, number, name or passage selected by earlier software. A selected item is not necessarily wrong.
The initial software stage, before any later AI inspection. Its changes and warnings remain recorded separately from accepted text.
Recorded positions and boundaries of the original OCR lines, used to check whether a split really crosses adjacent lines.
One model request covering related flagged items in the same assigned passage, rather than a separate call for each flag.
Connecting the software stages and testing them locally without sending a new request to an AI model.
Test answers deliberately written to exercise software behavior. They are not new answers returned by an AI experiment.
A check that the requested reading appears once between unchanged nearby source text. Changed or repeated nearby text can make the check inconclusive.
A source link covering a whole paragraph instead of claiming an exact match for each changed word.
A proposed text that software can reproduce exactly from the original text and a recorded replacement. This does not establish accuracy against the image.
Markers that select passages containing possible numbers for image inspection; they do not declare the numbers wrong.
Information from a word or name list that helps choose what to inspect, without proving what the original page says.
A claim about which particular words in one text correspond to words in another text.
Short names identifying the assigned passages. They distinguish those passages from nearby context.
A newly started program that reads saved work, rather than relying on the earlier program’s memory.
A saved record that the owned request has stopped. It is separate from saving the returned words.
A reply that provides no proposed reading and explains why the evidence is uncertain.
Amounts expressed indirectly through surrounding language rather than a straightforward numeric form.
A disagreement about how an answer must be represented, separate from whether its proposed words match the source.
A short message saying that the task is finished. Here it is separate from a proposed historical reading.
A requirement about the structure or fields of an answer, such as when a field must contain no value.
A check applied by the local software after a model returns an answer.
Counted and returned by the model-running software; this is not an independent measurement of its internal input representation.
A case already seen during development or earlier feedback, so it cannot serve as a new blind quality test.
The local request program responsible for the private model process it starts and stops.
The machine-readable description of the fields and value types allowed in a model reply.
A proposed corrected-text output produced after validation; it still needs any required source-quality or human acceptance.
The required arrangement and values of answer fields, separate from whether the proposed historical words are accurate.
A reason field containing JSON null, meaning no explanation of uncertainty is supplied. It is different from the string “null” or an empty string.
An answer claiming to cover the entire assigned passage. Here it must contain text and a null reason; that claim alone does not prove accuracy.
An authored demonstration of how a reply should withhold text when the evidence cannot support a complete reading.
An example deliberately written by the agent to exercise a software rule. It is not an observation returned by a model or made from an actual scan.
Made-up situations presented to explain or test behavior, without claiming that they occurred in the source material.

Permission for this one experiment to proceed before an exact measurement of how the model represents the image and text internally. It does not increase the model’s real capacity or approve a full run.
The size of the model’s actual internal representation of the supplied image and words; reported word counts alone may not measure it.
A saved record allowing at most one attempt. Once claimed, it remains spent even if the request fails.
Saving the exact program and request settings that a particular run is allowed to use.
A check that proposed text stays within the one assigned source passage rather than copying nearby text.
A missing or inadequate connection between a proposed reading and the exact source passage it claims to represent.
Words visible beside or around the assigned passage, which may belong to another paragraph.
A saved example of an actual or specified failure used to check that a later software change catches it.
An observed reply following the fields required for a complete reading. It does not by itself prove that the reading is accurate or stays within its source boundaries.
Only some of a source passage is present in the supplied picture. The unseen remainder must not be presented as if it was inspected.
A proposed reading containing only the assigned passage, without adding nearby context.
Nearby source words present in the image and supplied for orientation. They are not part of the text requested for repair.
Agreement with the original source in wording, scope and meaning. A text-format or copied-line check alone cannot establish it.
Positions recorded for text on the source page, used here to locate it within the saved picture.
In this check, a hyphen or a space between the same words is treated alike. Joined or rewritten words are not automatically treated as identical.
Writing down the words visible in an image.
The point where printed text continues on the next line. A line break can occur within one paragraph.
Mostly the same words and order, while some characters or words may still need repair.
How closely repeated runs on the same inputs agree. Agreement alone does not show that the reading matches the original page.
Separate model calls that each receive the same input and no earlier reply in their conversation. They may still share the same model and computer.
The fixed repeated calls included before the experiment starts. These are observations of variation, rather than replacements chosen after seeing an error.
Evidence that the model’s own image and text representation fits its available capacity. Counting the visible text alone does not establish this.
The latest time allowed for the entire set of repeated calls and its final report. It cannot be reset between repetitions.
A page layout with two vertical blocks of text. The reading may continue from the bottom of one block to the top of the next.
Numbers written with letters such as I, V, X, L and C. For example, XIII means thirteen.
Words from a law reproduced inside another passage, rather than the surrounding speaker’s own narration.
Software instructions that apply the same specified text operation each time, without asking a language model.
Example readings prepared after looking at the original scan. They remain proposals unless independently checked or accepted.
Prepared with earlier human comments included in the model’s instructions. This does not test what the model would notice without those comments.
Whether the returned reply passes the software’s required format and source-link checks. Passing does not prove every word is accurate.
The recorded stopping of the model processes started for this test. It does not refer to other running services.
The measured time for one model request to return, including the work counted by the runner’s timer.
A limit that would prevent a request from being sent if its input exceeded the stated size.
The complete internal size of the image and text has not been measured for the model.
Using exactly the same source, picture, instructions and settings in each repeated call.
Amounts expressed in words, such as two or three, rather than digits.
The exact characters returned by the model, including spaces and line breaks. Replies can differ in layout while proposing the same reading.
A judgment made by the AI agent after comparing the evidence. It is not a human review or automatic approval.
A reference reading produced and checked by people without relying on the tested model’s answer. It is used for comparison rather than assumed from model agreement.
A change adopted into the collection’s text. A model proposal alone does not make that change.
The maximum time permitted for one described task or request. More allowed time is not a promise that it will finish.
Able to restore exactly the information supplied before the change of format. This does not show that the source information is accurate.
Turning a stored representation back into the information it represents.
The parts of the assigned material that a reviewer or model says it checked. A claim of coverage does not prove the check was accurate.
A check that the model’s complete internal image and text representation fits its available capacity. Counting the visible text alone does not establish this.
How faithfully results represent original writing across the whole collection. Selected examples do not establish this rate.
Token totals were not returned or verified for an attempt. This does not mean that no work or cost occurred.
Using original material as the basis for a check. The conclusion still depends on what was inspected.
The largest model reply allowed for a request, measured here in tokens. Reaching it can cut a reply off.
A rule applied to a complete piece of text, such as an entire word or sentence. A string is a stored piece of text.
A compact rule describing allowed text. For example, a rule may allow a full sentence but reject a reply containing only spaces.
A difference between how two parts of a program interpret the same rule. It is a possible explanation to check, not a confirmed cause.
A model receives the page image without an OCR text copy or an older proposed transcription. It can still use patterns learned during training.
One tiny dot in a digital image. Pixel coordinates locate a position by counting dots from the image edge.
The rectangular area selected for inspection. Its left, top, right and bottom edges identify the requested area in the image.
A copied image area keeps every original decoded pixel value. This describes the copying process, not a model’s ability to read the print.
A digital image file format that can store pixel values without losing detail during encoding.
